meta.note: Values below are representative handbook/typical-batch figures (comparable to MMPDS, MatWeb, and standard aerospace materials references), not a specific mill certification. Real properties vary by heat treatment, batch, test temperature, and manufacturer -- verify against a datasheet before citing an exact number to a HAL panel. All values room-temperature unless otherwise noted.

items.garun_relevance: The default choice if your conceptual layout (§11) needs a specific material called out for engine-mount brackets or high-load fittings near the rear-fuselage engine/generator cluster.
items.description: The single most-used titanium alloy in aerospace, accounting for roughly half of all titanium aerospace tonnage -- excellent strength-to-weight ratio and good high-temperature performance relative to aluminum.

items.garun_relevance: Higher-temperature-capable option than Ti-6Al-4V for compressor-section components ahead of the superalloy hot section, if the propulsion model is ever extended beyond a BSFC lookup.
items.description: Retains useful strength up to ~500 C, filling the gap between Ti-6Al-4V's ~400 C ceiling and where nickel superalloys become necessary.

items.garun_relevance: Low-strength but highly corrosion-resistant and easily formable -- relevant only for non-load-bearing ducting (e.g. exhaust shrouding) rather than structural members.
items.description: Not an alloy in the strength sense -- valued for corrosion resistance, weldability, and formability rather than mechanical performance.

items.garun_relevance: Highest-strength titanium option if the CG/structural discussion (§11.3) needs a specific high-load fastener or landing-gear material called out.
items.description: Cold-formable in the solution-treated condition then age-hardened to very high strength -- a common landing-gear and fastener alloy where Ti-6Al-4V's strength isn't quite enough.
